newsitem.title: UK: S&P says may cut English China Clay ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P says may cut English China Clay ratings.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Monday it placed both its A plus and A1 ratings of English China Clays PLC and its related entity English China Clays Delaware Inc. on Creditwatch with negative implications.

"This followed the announcement by ECC of significantly lower than expected interim results, with operating profit from continuing operations in the first half of 1996 deteriorating to 30 million stg ($46 million), compared with 56 million stg in the same period one year earlier," S&P said in a statement.

S&P said operating exceptionals reduced income further by 18 million stg. It said the reduction was principally due to severe trading conditions caused by low operating rates in the forest products industry, which accounts for around 70 percent of ECC's sales, as well as manufacturing efficiency problems in one area of the group's business.

"As a consequence, cash flow has declined substantially to an outflow in the first half of 1996 (including paid out dividend of 34 million stg), compared with an inflow in the same period one year prior," S&P said.
The rating agency said ECC's net debt has risen to 215 million stg at June 30, 1996, compared with 189 million stg at financial year-end 1995.
